text:
alex: Quick API Q — before we lock v2 routing contract: what exactly wins when clients send model_id vs model_hint vs fallback_model? Need behavior spelled out for Hosted + Dedicated + Private. CC @maya @pranav

maya: High level: model_id is authoritative. If model_id present we try to serve that exact variant (or compatible binary) in the selected pool. model_hint is a soft preference used only when model_id is missing to choose a compatible candidate. fallback_model is an explicit override used when the primary selection fails (capacity/compat). Dedicated pools will not automatically cross customer pools for a fallback unless allow_fallback:true on the dedicated config. Hosted will follow the fallback chain by default.

pranav: To add: we have a compatibility matrix for tokenizer/kv-cache format. If model_id points to a variant with incompatible KV format we should error with 409 + explanation rather than silently fallback. Do we want automatic compatibility conversions?

maya: We currently do NOT convert KV formats automatically. Policy: incompatible primary -> return 409 with body explaining "incompatible_model_kv_format" and suggest a compatible model_hint/fallback_model. We will only auto-fallback for cases where the binary is compatible but the exact variant is unavailable (e.g., quantized vs fp).

alex: Can we capture the contract as a minimal example? e.g. the router behavior in order:
```json
{
  "priority": ["model_id", "model_hint", "default_catalog_hint"],
  "fallback_order": ["fallback_model", "same_region_compatible", "cross_region_compatible"],
  "errors": {"incompatible_kv": 409, "no_capacity": 503}
}
```
This way SDKs can implement client-side logic.

julie: FYI PR #4821 updates fallback order to prefer same-region different-tier before cross-region. Pinged @eng-oncall and reviewers. Link: https://phabricator.redwood/4821 (staging only atm). :eyes:

deploy-bot: PR #4821 merged into staging by julie — smoke tests running.

diego: One more question: region/tier hints from clients. If a client supplies region_hint="eu" and tier="premium" should router strictly prefer eu-premium, and only fall back to global-premium if latency SLO violated? Or is cross-tier allowed earlier?

maya: Router policy: prefer same region/tier first. If same region premium is saturated then, depending on customer allow_fallback_policy, we try same region lower tier (if allowed), then same tier cross-region (if latency budget allows), then global best-effort. Customers can set allow_cross_region:false to prevent cross-region. We'll add a matrix in the doc.

pranav: Back-compat note: accept legacy param `model` as alias for model_id for 6 months. Add response warning header `X-Deprecation-Model` with a timestamp and link to migration guide. Also recommend returning a telemetry flag so SDKs can log and migrate.

alex: Sounds good. I'll draft the API contract section and open a tiny PR to add the header + mapping. Tagging @julie for release notes and @diego for router tests.

julie: ack — will add a short blurb to the release draft and schedule a quick playbook update for Dedicated customers who have strict fallback rules.

alex: Thanks all — if nobody objects I'll merge the contract PR tomorrow AM and coordinate with QA for a small compatibility test matrix. :thumbsup:
